title: Algorithms for Interviews
units/0/blurb: The method the whole course builds on: complexity and Big-O in practice, what the constraints let you afford, the cost of .NET collections, allocations and recursion in C# and Unity, how to reason out loud, and the usual mistakes.
units/1/blurb: Trade memory for time: Two Sum, duplicates, anagrams, prefix sums in a dictionary, a set as an accelerator and an array as a hash table. How Dictionary works in .NET and what GetHashCode costs on a struct.
units/2/blurb: Compacting an array without allocations, converging pointers and why they lose nothing, trapping rain water, rotating and spiralling a matrix, a tile grid in memory and an in-place cellular automaton.
units/3/blurb: Fixed and variable windows, a window with a counter, Minimum Window Substring and the sliding window maximum on a monotonic deque. Why .NET has no Deque<T> and what to use instead.
units/4/blurb: Masks and bit counting, XOR, bits as a table, arithmetic without operators and maximum XOR. In games: layer masks, flags, bitboards and autotiles; BitOperations in .NET and math in Unity.
units/5/blurb: Matching brackets and a min stack, the monotonic stack, reversing and merging lists, fast and slow pointers, reversing in groups. LinkedList<T> from the inside and an allocation-free list on indices.
units/6/blurb: Boundary invariants without off-by-one errors, the rotated array, searching on the answer, the median of two arrays. For games: a weighted loot table and a fair Fisher–Yates shuffle.
units/7/blurb: How .NET sorts and when you do not need to, merging and inserting intervals, one-pass greedy, Kadane, and how to prove a greedy solution is correct.
units/8/blurb: A size-k heap versus quickselect, frequencies and nearest points, merging k lists and a streaming median. PriorityQueue in .NET 6+ and your own heap for Unity.
units/9/blurb: Recursion and level order, validating a BST, LCA and maximum path sum: return one thing, update another. Walking a Transform hierarchy without recursion.
units/10/blurb: A grid as a graph, multi-source BFS, topological sort, state-space graphs and Union-Find. Tile flood fill, distance maps, system initialization order and procedural caves.
units/11/blurb: What game dev interviews actually ask: Dijkstra, minimax paths, A* on a grid, flow fields for crowds of units and spatial partitioning with grids, hashes and quadtrees. With Jobs and Burst where they belong.
units/12/blurb: Decision trees, pruning, from recursion to a table, the unbounded knapsack, DP on two strings and LIS in O(n log n). How to spot DP in a problem and name the state and the transition.
units/13/title: Data structure design and final exam
units/13/blurb: LRU and LFU, the trie, tree serialization, object pools and ring buffers, from the LeetCode problem to an asset cache in a game. Then the exam on the whole course.
